findings.text: The nested exit helper publishes committed second level guest state into the first level control block addressed by the stored nested GPA. It maps that block for local access and propagates segmentation and descriptor state, paging and feature controls, execution position and privilege, debug state, plus exit reason and interrupt state from the active shadow block and architected vCPU state. PAT, CET state, next RIP and branch record state apply only when feature or mode checks allow. A pending event is encoded into exit information unless the exit indicates VMRUN failure. Injection fields are cleared, interrupt control is restored from cached nested controls, and the exit is traced.

When recording a pending event into L1 exit information, injected exception outranks injected NMI, which outranks injected interrupt. Exceptions carry vector with valid and exception type marking plus optional error code and error valid marking. NMIs carry valid and NMI type marking without vector. Interrupts carry vector with valid marking and a soft versus hardware type distinction. Absence of all three yields a zeroed field.
Whether an exit code denotes VMRUN failure is decided by equality against the architected error code, narrowed to the low 32 bits when running under a hypervisor and full width otherwise.

Nested virtualization keeps three related containers: the L1 owned block, the active shadow block used for second level execution, and a cached copy of L1 nested controls. The save partition carries CPU state such as segmentation, tables, paging and feature controls, debug and branch records, and CET state. The control partition carries exit reason, exit details, interrupt state and injection controls. On exit, save and selected control state move from shadow to L1, while virtual interrupt state and injection details are reconciled from cached controls.

Writes to the extended feature enable register form an entry point owning nested context lifetime. Without nested paging the effective value forces execute disable semantics and drops long mode enable when long mode active is clear. A change in the secure virtual machine enable bit provisions or abandons nested state, refreshes performance counter programming and requests intercept recalculation. The hardware control block always records the enable bit as set and is marked dirty in the control register group.

Nested context follows uninitialized, initialized, and active in guest states. Provisioning is idempotent and allocates a shadow control page plus an MSR permission bitmap, recording the shadow physical address with memory encryption adjustment. Release returns to uninitialized, restoring the primary control block when needed, freeing both allocations and invalidating the cached L1 GPA optimization. Switching the current block pointer selects which container hardware uses.

The permission map allocator provides intercept bitmaps for MSR and IO virtualization. It allocates enough contiguous pages for the requested size, fails with null when memory is unavailable, and initializes every bit to set so all accesses intercept unless explicitly allowed. Release frees the same page order derived from the MSR map size.

Shadow control pages for nested and potentially shielded guests come from a single zeroed page allocated on the current NUMA node with accounted kernel memory. The node specific helper centralizes zeroing and order zero allocation, and the node agnostic wrappers resolve the current node.

Forced departure from nested mode leaves no nested residue: guest mode is exited, the stored L1 GPA becomes invalid, the primary control block becomes current and fully dirty, nested address translation context is discarded, global interrupt handling is re enabled, and performance and virtual APIC refreshes are scheduled through deferred mechanisms. Clearing of the nested state pages request holds regardless of prior guest mode membership.

Global interrupt flag virtualization has software and hardware forms. When virtual GIF support is disabled globally, the flag lives in a software boolean. When enabled, it lives in the GIF bit of a selected control block: the shadow block while in nested mode without nested virtual GIF enable, otherwise the primary block. Nested virtual GIF enable requires both guest capability and a control bit in cached nested controls. Enabling drops stale virtual interrupt and STGI intercepts and schedules event processing if work is pending; disabling blocks interrupts and manages the virtual interrupt intercept according to virtual GIF mode.

A global interrupt enable transition treats system management, non maskable, maskable, and APIC initialization or startup requests as wakeup sources. Pending work in any of those classes causes the enable path to request event injection processing.

Nested transitions reprogram performance counters from a mask of mode sensitive enables. The immediate form suits architected transitions so the triggering instruction counts in the new mode, while the deferred form suits forced non architected departure to avoid touching performance state from arbitrary contexts.

Secure guest detection has two build dependent forms sharing one name: one reports the active state recorded in confidential computing info attached to the VM, the other is a constant false stub. Callers use it to exempt shielded guests from erratum workarounds that would require reading guest memory.

Exception intercepts are owned by the primary control block. Setting or clearing a vector adjusts the exception intercept bitmap at an offset derived from the vector number, validates the vector range with a one time warning, and marks intercept state dirty for later reconciliation.

Virtualized branch record support is enabled when the current control block requests branch tracing or when nested mode is active with guest branch virtualization capability and nested enablement. Transitions set or clear a miscellaneous control bit, with disabling forbidden for certain shielded guests. Regardless of whether the enable bit changed, MSR intercept state for branch record and last exception address registers, plus debug control for shielded guests, is reconciled so virtualized access is direct and non virtualized access intercepts. Current intercept polarity is cached to avoid redundant updates.

TSC scaling updates are guarded against preemption and apply only when guest state is loaded. The low level writer elides the model specific register write when the requested ratio already matches the per CPU cached ratio, otherwise it writes and updates the cache.

Control register virtualization separates architected guest values from host effective values written to hardware. On 64 bit hosts, long mode active follows paging transitions while long mode enable is set. Without nested paging, the host value forces paging, write protect and address extension bits and suppresses supervisor protections and key protections when paging is off, and a paging mode change triggers resynchronization of the other register. Firmware quirks may clear cache disable and not write through bits, and host machine check enable is merged into the host value. The control register group is marked dirty. Shielded guests keep CR intercepts cleared; otherwise CR0 intercepts track equality between host and guest values, and changes to save restore or key protection bits flag dynamic CPUID bits dirty.

Whether nested execution exits on physical interrupts is vendor specific: the SVM form consults the cached L1 intercept bitmap for the interrupt bit, while the VMX form consults pin based execution controls of the cached second level control structure for the external interrupt mask. The VMX cache is reached through a container conversion from vCPU to vendor state with a lock ownership assertion.

Virtualized APIC updates require the VM read side APIC update lock with preemption disabled and are skipped without an in kernel APIC. Activation holds exactly when no VM wide or vCPU specific inhibit reasons are set and the APIC operating mode is not disabled. On polarity change the LAPIC active flag, LAPIC virtualization state and execution controls are refreshed, and deactivation schedules event processing to drain interrupts that arrived while virtualization was active.

On nested exit an indirect branch barrier is required unless hardware reports same mode branch immunity, and then only when the guest exposes speculation control or AMD branch prediction features. Separately, a debug check warns when a nested run remains flagged as pending at a point where it must have been consumed.

Several paths carry correctness hazards: clearing secure virtual machine enable while nested and runnable synthesizes a triple fault to avoid executing second level code in first level context; freeing nested state invalidates a GPA based clean field optimization; fully clearing the clean bitmap forces reload of all fields; virtual interrupt clearing asserts task priority consistency between shadow and cached controls; disabling branch virtualization is illegal for shielded guests; and exception vector updates are range checked.

Host invoked update entry points refresh virtualized state outside direct guest writes: global interrupt flag control, branch virtualization enablement, TSC scaling, control register shadowing, and virtual APIC activation. Each reconciles hardware control fields, intercept bitmaps or cached state and schedules follow up requests where architectural effects may be pending.

Symbolic control selectors for dirty group tracking, intercept selection, quirk selection, feature bits and exit codes are opaque names shared with hardware and generic KVM layers; the fragments use them to select fields and modes but do not define numeric values. The SVM HyperV header carries a conventional include guard macro to ensure single inclusion.
